**Run and test**
- `npm run dev:test` → http://localhost:3000 against the **test** project (`/play`, `/dev/screens?s=<screen>` for every screen with sample data). Plain `npm run dev` uses `.env.local`'s **production** keys — avoid it for trying things out.
- `npm test` (unit + screens) · `npm run test:integration` (live, test project) · `npm run e2e` (real browser plays a round on the test project) · `npm run e2e:admin` (real browser runs a whole hunt from /admin on the test project) · `npm run screens` (screenshots for comparing with the canvas) · `npm run build` / `lint` / `typecheck`.

**Database changes:** new file `supabase/migrations/00NN_*.sql` → `supabase db push` (test) → tests green → `supabase link --project-ref vwkggtlrypmhlhifveob` → `supabase db push` → `supabase link --project-ref ljvgprlnbufbgcdwrupf` (back to test). Edge Function: `supabase functions deploy player-join --project-ref <ref> --use-api`.

**Gotchas learned**
- Supabase grants EXECUTE on every new function to `anon`/`authenticated` by default: each new RPC needs an explicit `revoke … from public, anon, authenticated` + `grant` (D-028, migration 0007).
- Whole-table `delete`/`update` from an RPC needs `where true` (Supabase safe-update guard).
- The Supabase MCP's `apply_migration` asks for a confirmation on SQL containing `delete` that this editor can't show (it comes back "declined"): apply migrations with the CLI.
- Player RPCs raise only guard errors (`NOT_REGISTERED`, `SESSION_MOVED`); game outcomes return `{ok:false, code}` so alerts aren't rolled back.

**Before P1 starts (setup):**
- Docs approved by the user.
- Credentials provided: Supabase prod and test projects, Vercel project.
- Blender MCP connected (configured in `.mcp.json`; Blender add-on "Connect" pressed).

Objective: Shared round-1 QRs so more than 10 teams fit the same 48 places (D-039) and a Game over pop-up for everyone (D-040), then a hand-written question bank and the location clues for the real venue.

**Build order:** T-508, T-509, T-501, T-502, T-506, T-511 done. Next T-507, then T-510 (routes far apart, D-042), then T-503 (clues for the 58 places in `docs/venue/locations.md`).

**Needed from the user before P5 can finish** (only T-503 and entering the places wait for these):
- **Every place**, as *building · floor · name*: rooms by number, libraries, labs, canteen, boys' hostel, and so on.
- **A hiding spot only for big places** (a library shelf, a hostel common room, "behind computer 12" in a lab). A normal room needs none: the room is the spot.
- **Enough places**: the game is sized for 10 teams, 15 → 9 → 6 → 4 → 3 → 2 → 1 = 40 marks + 8 decoys = **48 places**, plus a few spare. More than 10 teams share the same 48 (D-039). With fewer places the generator refuses the course.
- **Optional, for better riddles**: what is in or near each place, names students use for it, landmarks.
- **Status (2026-10-26):** list received — 59 places in `docs/venue/locations.md` (43 in the Main Engineering Block, 16 outside), with a few points still to confirm (see 'Where we are' item 3); the satellite screenshots are in `docs/venue/`. With the list, Claude writes the clue sets (T-503) and the questions stay the shared bank (D-036).
- **How to send it**: a plain list in chat is fine, one place per line, e.g. `Main block · 2nd floor · Room 204` or `Library · ground floor · Library — hide behind shelf C3`. Then say **"continue"**.
- ~~Expected team count~~ settled: designed for 10; up to 15 fit as is, beyond 15 teams share round-1 QRs (D-039).
- ~~Question topics~~ settled: general, clean humour, no campus in-jokes (D-036).

## P8 · Simulation, hardening & release
Status: PLANNED · Depends: P3–P7 · Paths: scripts/**, integration/**, docs/** · Flags: testing, security · Evidence: —
Objective: Prove the hunt end-to-end with bots at more than the expected crowd (25 teams, everyone joining at once from one IP), attack it with every cheat and security hole we know, check every rule independently, record it all on video, and list **every flaw** in one report, then fix and rerun until runs are clean. After that, test on real phones at the venue.

**One command runs everything:** `npm run bots` (T-809) → every check below, in order, against the **test** project only, then the 4-screen `demo.mp4` and the flaw report. Bot tests use **Python scripts** (`scripts/sim/`, own venv + `requirements.txt`); browsers are Playwright.

**Build order:** T-801 → T-810 → T-806 → T-809 → T-807 (repeat until clean) → T-808 → T-802 → T-803 → T-804 → T-805.

**Rules every run checks** (the rule checker, T-810, reads them back from the database after the run, independently of the game code):

| Rule | What is checked |
|---|---|
| Elimination (D-012) | Each round: exactly X crews complete; the eliminated set is exactly the crews still in that round at the moment the X-th completes; a crew finishing after the round closed is eliminated, not advanced; lowering X live closes the round at once |
| Ties at the X-th slot (T9) | Several crews check in in the same second at the X-th slot: still exactly X advance |
| Hint penalty (D-041) | +1:00 per hint, never on multiple choice |
| Wrong-answer penalty (D-041) | For multiple choice **and** typed answers: every 3rd wrong on a player's question adds +1:00 (3rd, 6th, 9th …); the count restarts each round; nobody is ever locked out; a wrong multiple-choice pick swaps the question and the old one never comes back to the crew |
| Penalty served (D-013) | Penalty = 1:00 × hints + 1:00 × ⌊wrongs ÷ 3⌋ per player, summed for the crew; the round counts at check-in + penalty; `complete_round` before then → PENALTY_RUNNING; pause freezes the countdown |
| Penalty and finish order | A crew that checks in first but carries a penalty is overtaken by a crew with none, and can be eliminated by it |
| Round lock (D-025) | A later-round QR or key never counts, and the early scan isn't remembered |
| Print cards (D-031, D-043) | Every card's cut-off stub names the right place (# · building · floor · place, hiding spot, landmark, matching `docs/venue/locations.md` and the database); the card part above the cut line shows nothing but brand, QR, scan note and key — no label, round, place or decoy word |
| Routes far apart (D-042) | No crew's route ever has two consecutive places in the same area (Main Block, MBA area, North, Boys' Hostel, SVIT Cafe) |
| Finish (D-026, D-040) | Final needs printed key + own seal code; podium = first 3 final completions; unique completion keys; Game over pop-up on every phone and the projector |
| Isolation | No response or realtime message to a player ever contains another crew's data, an answer, a key, a token, a seal code or a place name before the fog lifts |

| ID | Task | Status | Depends | Capabilities | Security | Design | Testing | Acceptance |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| T-801 | Bot simulation in Python (`scripts/sim/simulate.py`): **25 teams × 4 = 100 bots** on the 10-team pyramid (round 1 capped at 15 and shared, D-039); **all 100 join in the same second from one IP**, like the event Wi-Fi; full hunt through the top 3 and the Game over pop-up. Bots are given personalities so every rule is used: careful (no misses), guessers (many wrong answers, typed and multiple choice, to earn wrong-answer penalties), hint takers, slow crews (to be eliminated), crews that tie at the X-th slot, prank-QR chasers. The admin bot pauses/resumes, changes X live, toggles hints, broadcasts, marks a member inactive, kicks one, re-points a crew | PLANNED | P2 | testing/strategy | Refuses the prod project; test project's Auth rate limits set to match prod first, so the join storm is a real test | — | — | 5/5 runs green with 25 teams; no join refused by a rate limit; every rule in the table above used at least once per run |
| T-810 | Rule checker (`scripts/sim/oracle.py`): after each run, rebuild the game from `events`, `round_results`, `tasks`, `team_state`, `checkins`, `admin_audit` and recheck every rule in the table above with its own Python code (not the engine's). Every mismatch is a finding with the crew, round, expected vs actual | PLANNED | T-801 | testing/strategy | Service role read-only, test project only | — | pytest on hand-made event logs (incl. a 3-wrong penalty and a tie at X) | A planted bug (e.g. hint = 2:00, or X + 1 advancing) is caught every time |
| T-806 | Cheating + security suite in Python (`scripts/sim/attacks/`), one test per attack, each run as a real player or anonymous caller. **Game cheats:** wrong team's QR; a later round's QR + its printed key; a round-3 QR scanned early, then later; prank QRs; guessing keys (5/min); brute-force answers (10/min) and checking the wrong-answer penalty still adds up while rate-limited; tapping every multiple-choice option; a foreign seal code at the final; a reused or made-up completion key; check-in without a scan; one member checking in for all four; a scan ticket replayed or used after 10 min; acting while paused; acting after elimination or after being kicked/marked inactive; finishing a penalty early by calling `complete_round` or faking the phone's clock; leaving the site while answering. **Joining:** a 5th member; one player on two phones; name takeover; a made-up team code; join flood from one IP; forged `ip` / `user_id` sent to `player-join`. **Access:** reading every table through the REST API as a player and as anon (questions, answers, qr_codes, keys, tokens, assignments, locations, other crews' tasks/team_state, `final_code`, `completion_key`); writing or deleting any row directly; calling every admin RPC and every internal helper (`_eliminate`, `_complete_round`, …) as a player and as anon; subscribing to other crews' realtime rows; uploading to or deleting from the venue Storage bucket; a tampered or expired JWT; a session kept after New Game. **Print sheet:** the QR sheet as a player and signed out (refused); every card part scanned for leaked label / round / place / "decoy" text; every stub checked against the place list. **Input:** SQL-injection and very long strings in names, answers, keys, broadcast; `<script>` and HTML in crew names, player names, broadcast and question text (must show as text); CSV import with formula cells (`=HYPERLINK…`) and bad rows. **Races:** two crews at the X-th slot in the same second; double `complete_round`; hint + answer at once; two phones of one player answering at once | PLANNED | T-801 | testing/strategy, engineering/security | T1–T20 | — | Python suite | Every attempt is refused and/or alerted exactly as the PRD and SECURITY.md say; none changes another crew's state; every threat T1–T20 has at least one attack |
| T-809 | `npm run bots` (`scripts/sim/run_all.py`): runs, in order, lint, typecheck, build, unit tests, integration tests, `e2e` + `e2e:admin`, the simulation (T-801), the rule checker (T-810), the attack suite (T-806), load (T-803), security scans (`npm audit`, `pip-audit`, bundle secret scan, Supabase security + performance advisors), then harvests logs (RPC errors, Supabase Postgres / Auth / Edge Function logs, every browser console) and records the demo (T-808). Never stops at the first failure: every step's result goes into the run folder `docs/reports/runs/<date-time>/` (summary, logs, screenshots of each failure, videos) and into the flaw report | PLANNED | T-806 | testing/strategy | Refuses prod keys; no prod codes or keys in any output | — | — | One command, one report; a planted failure in any step shows up in the report |
| T-807 | Find–fix–recheck loop: run `npm run bots`; every problem becomes a finding in **`docs/reports/flaws.md`**: ID, severity (blocker / major / minor / cosmetic), area (rules, security, UI, performance, content), what happened, how to reproduce, where it shows (log line, screenshot, demo timestamp), fix, retest result. Fix, rerun everything, repeat | PLANNED | T-809 | testing/strategy | — | — | Python suite | Two clean full runs in a row; every finding is fixed and retested, or accepted by the user in writing |
| T-808 | `docs/demo/demo.mp4`: **four screens in a 2 × 2 grid, recorded at the same time**: the **admin panel** (live dashboard: crews, alerts, log, X), and **three phones** from different crews. Playwright drives them; Chromium's fake camera plays each printed QR into the in-site scanner, so the real scanner reads it. Captions name each step: join, universal QR, solve (a wrong answer, the 3rd miss adding +1:00), hint (+1:00), scan + key, penalty countdown, round complete, a crew eliminated when X is reached (its phone shows Eliminated, the admin card goes red), a cheat refused and its admin alert, final with seal code, top 3, Game over on every screen. A full-length version (`demo-full.mp4`) of every run is kept in the run folder so mistakes can be found by timestamp. Shows the site's scanner, not real phone cameras (T-804 covers those) | PLANNED | T-807 | testing/release-verification | Test project only; no real codes or keys from prod | — | — | User has watched the video |
| T-802 | Security review of anything T-806 can't automate: RLS policies and grants read line by line, CSP and headers, dependency audit triage, secret scan of repo history | PLANNED | T-807 | engineering/security | T1–T20 | — | integration | All security tests green; review notes in `docs/reports/flaws.md` |
| T-803 | Load: 30 teams × 4 bots concurrently from one IP on the 48 places (D-039), with the admin dashboard and projector open | PLANNED | T-801 | engineering/performance | — | — | — | p95 RPC < 500 ms; no 5xx, no rate-limit refusals; dashboard stays live |
| T-804 | REAL_DEVICE_TEST.md run at the venue (signal at every spot, iOS + Android scanners) | PLANNED | T-802 | testing/release-verification | — | — | manual log | No blocking issue |
